tools.name: compare_with_human
tools.description: Shows two options (texts, images, videos, audio clips or web pages) side by side to a verified human and returns which one they prefer ("A", "B" or "tie") with a short reason. Use it when a choice depends on taste, clarity or feel and you want a real person to decide: two logo drafts, two headlines,

tools.name: rate_with_human
tools.description: Shows one piece of work (text, image, video, audio or web page) to a verified human and returns a score from 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent) with written feedback on what works and what to fix. Use it to check whether something you produced is actually good before you deliver it: an email that must sound

tools.name: get_human_feedback
tools.description: Returns the current state of a task you created earlier with compare_with_human or rate_with_human, and its result once a human has answered. findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "compare_with_human" appears informational but accepts parameters (context) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "rate_with_human" appears informational but accepts parameters (context) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: compare_with_human, rate_with_human, get_account · Private data: get_account · Public sink: compare_with_human, rate_with_human, get_account.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: compare_with_human, rate_with_human, get_account · Private data: get_account · Public sink: compare_with_human, rate_with_human, get_account

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
